utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-95-14 & 14/2-R77, the Prosecutor versus Josip Jovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Jovic, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May I then have the appearances, Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: On behalf of the Prosecution, David Akerson, and I'm here with Rebecca Graham, Salvatore Cannata, and the case manager Sebastian van Hooydonk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Akerson. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I'm Kresimir Krsnik. I am a member of the Croatian bar association, and I'm lead counsel in the case against Mr. Jovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krsnik. The purpose of this Article 62 hearing is to formally charge you, Mr. Jovic, and to introduce the next step in the proceedings which is to hear how you plead in relation to these charges. I do understand, Mr. Jovic, that Mr. Krsnik is your counsel who will help you in these proceedings; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovic, have you received a copy of the indictment in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovic, did you have an opportunity to discuss the content of this indictment with counsel?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have had an opportunity to discuss that with my counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you were able to fully understand the charges that were brought against you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I was able to understand them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, since you responded to a motion filed by the Prosecution for joinder of several contempt cases, I take it that you're aware of this motion which has not yet been decided. Mr. Akerson, is it a correct understanding that the joinder of the cases will result in a new indictment but not in any new charges against this accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll then proceed on the basis of the existing indictment. Mr. Krsnik, have you discussed with Mr. Jovic whether he wants the indictment to be read out aloud to him?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is no need for that. Mr. Jovic has been informed of the details, so there's no need to read the indictment today. I wanted to say something else, Your Honour. We received a motion for joinder, but we have decided to file an objection this motion, and in keeping with that we will -- we shall await the decision of the Honourable Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Jovic, you are invited to plead on the indictment within 30 days, but if you choose to enter a plea today, I'll read the count, the one and only count of the indictment to you and invite you to enter a plea. Do you want to do that at a later stage, within 30 days, or would you prefer to enter a plea today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Today, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Jovic, I'll read the count to you, but I'll briefly repeat what -- what the charges are about. The charges deal with you knowingly and wilfully interfering with the administration of justice by publishing the identity of a protected ICTY witness, by publishing the fact that he testified in closed session, and by publishing excerpts of that testimony and by violating a court order issued in relation with that. I'll read the count to you. That is contempt of the Tribunal, punishable under the Tribunal's inherent power, Rule 77(A), Rule 77(A)(ii), and Rule 77(A)(iv), I should have said 77(A)(ii) and then 77(A)(iv), of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal. May I invite you to plead, to tell me whether you plead guilty or not guilty to this count.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then for the Trial Chamber it's recorded that you pleaded not guilty to the one and only count of the indictment brought against you. Usually under Rule 64, once an accused has appeared initially before this Tribunal, an order for remand -- for detention on remand will be issued. The Chamber has considered the matter and finds it disproportionate to order your detention on remand. So I will refrain from that, explicitly refrain from that. The warrant of arrest which has been issued against you, served for the purposes of your appearance today, that is for your appearance before this Tribunal and for your return to the state from which you came, that means that once you are returned that you'll be free to go. This, of course, does not mean that you're free to do whatever you want, because there's a general rule, both for accused and non-accused, not to interfere with witnesses, not to unduly influence the course of justice. Therefore, I would like to remind you that you're under an obligation in this respect as well as anyone else is. Mr. Jovic, this time you are summoned to appear, you prefer not to appear, then a warrant of arrest was issued. Finally you're here. I don't know whether on any future summons you will take the same course or that you again would prefer not to come and -- it might not come as a surprise to you that there's a fair chance that another warrant of arrest will be issued if you repeat the same conduct. Perhaps your counsel would like to say something about that, because he raised his hand. Mr. Krsnik, is there anything you'd like to submit in respect of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, just briefly. I Would like to clarify the situation, because I think that we may have been misunderstood. In our country, there is the constitutional law on cooperation with The Hague Tribunal. In my first motion I wanted to explain the position of my client, and I believe that I -- we explained our position very briefly. I said in this motion that we respect in Tribunal and that we will respond to every call by this Tribunal. However, since we are not dealing with a war crime, I don't want to go into any legal discussions because this is neither the time or the place, we wanted to use this constitutional law before the Supreme Court of the Republic of Croatia. We wanted to await their decision in which they will either confirm the position that this Tribunal is not competent to hold this trial or the contrary. And after that decision, we would have responded to the call from this Tribunal. What I'm saying here is that from this day on, we will respond to every call by the Tribunal, because Mr. Jovic has come here voluntarily. We will not deal with this issue before our courts. We will deal with this issue here before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see a change of position, a clear change of position where initially you took the position that a challenge of the jurisdiction of this Tribunal should be decided by the domestic courts in Croatia rather than by this Tribunal itself. Now, from what I understand, there might not have been any misunderstanding at that moment. It was perfectly clear, but you've changed your mind to the effect that you're now -- that you'll now accept a decision of this Tribunal on jurisdiction over this case. I also observed that there was not --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I did not mean to interrupt you. When this comes to competence, we shall deal this issue in our subsequent motions, and we will raise this legal matter, but when we do that it will be before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As you said before, "We will not deal with this issue before our courts, we will deal with this issue here before this Tribunal." The Chamber would have preferred that the accused would have take then position right away which would have prevented us to issue an arrest warrant. I also then do understand that any further summons to appear will be followed immediately without -- by your nodding, yes, I do understand that that's the present position of the accused and the Defence. Mr. Jovic, and Mr. Krsnik, although the issue of health usually is of more importance if someone is detained, I nevertheless want to raise it. Is there anything in your health or any personal circumstances the Chamber should know about? If so, please tell me, and if you'd prefer to deal with the matter in private session so that the audience will not hear it, please apply for private session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I don't have any health problems which would pose an obstacle to my participation in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's always good to hear that someone is free of health problems, Mr. Jovic. Then this concludes this Initial Appearance. Upon a plea of not guilty usually a day will be set for trial, but it's also common practice that it's not done immediately, but that is dependent on scheduling considerations and especially in this case where still a decision has to be taken on the motion for joinder, and where you have applied in your response to that motion to first receive supporting material, a date cannot be set by the Registry at this very moment, but Registry will do so in due course. Mr. Akerson, as far as the disclosure of supporting material is concerned, it would be very practical, of course, if you would have it ready so that Mr. Krsnik could receive it immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. There is -- we're happy to provide that today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: I'll make arrangements after this hearing with Mr. Krsnik. There is the bar on disclosure that you would need to lift in order for us to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's lifted, orally by this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there anything else to be raised?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: A few other matters, Your Honour. First of all, the time for preliminary motions in the other matter in the case against Mr. Krizic the time was set at ten days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was at a moment when we had a different expectation of when to hear the case. Let me first ask, Mr. Krsnik, do you intend to file any preliminary motions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you tell us what motions you would have in mind? Is it about the form of the indictment? Is it about any other preliminary -- is it about jurisdiction?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In any case, we will use Rule 73 first to deal with the issue of competence of the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Jurisdiction. Let me -- are you -- are you aware of the case law of this Tribunal on two matters, the first whether in contempt cases preliminary motions on jurisdiction can be received, and the second issue, the case law on jurisdiction, case law by the Appeals Chamber on the inherent powers already from the Tadic case to hear contempt cases, also not, of course, being one of the crimes under Articles 2, 3, 4 and 5 of the Statute? You're fully aware of that. Since you indicated that you want to file a preliminary motion on jurisdiction, what -- what are the reasons why you would depart from the existing case law although not from the Appeals Chamber on filing preliminary motions on jurisdiction in contempt cases?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have studied the case law, and as you know I've been defending the accused before this court for a number of years, and when I studied the case law when it comes to contempt, I have not come across a final decision. We have only had the first-instance court decisions on jurisdiction. Only a few days ago I filed a few interlocutory appeals against my motions in which why I raised the issue of jurisdictions -- jurisdiction, and I received the decisions of the Chamber. If I had a final decision, and if I -- if I knew the law of this, I would not decide to do that unless it went against the merit of the case. And one more thing. We would like to clarify one more thing when it comes to the case law. The position has its position, but we're waiting for the decision. Our learned friends from the Prosecution are not authorised to issue contempt indictments of their own will. As Article 77(B) says, it is only the Trial Chamber that is authorised to do that and only upon the decision of the Chamber can the Prosecutor act with such an indictment. And this is certainly a legal issue that has to be resolved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say you have got documents to file to such preliminary motions. We'll see what happens. How much time you think you'd need for those motions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In any case by the end of next week I'll be able to complete them. We have been waiting for this Initial Appearance to take place. As soon as I come back from -- to Croatia I will start working on them, and I believe I will finish within ten to 15 days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Without any -- you said by the end of next week. Without giving any indication on whether the motions and dependent on the subjects you'd like to raise could be received, the date, the time limit for preliminary motions is set to Wednesday, the 26th of October. So please keep in mind that they should be filed by then. Any other issue, Mr. Akerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: I need to go back to the disclosure of supporting materials. The one thing I need to ask the Court to do is to make sure that the accused and his counsel knows that the Court -- or I need the Court to instruct them that they're not to disclose it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Once disclosed, there is now an additional order for you to -- although the disclosure is now permitted, that you should not in the terms as usually put in written decisions, you should not disclose the content to the public, to any third party. It's for the accused and the Defence and for no one else. Mr. Akerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: One last issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: The Prosecution received a motion from this accused, I think two days ago, maybe yesterday, and it is a request for certification of interlocutory appeal to challenge the decision to deny the Defence's motion for rescission of warrant of arrest and order for surrender. The Prosecution is deeming this to be moot now. I've spoken to Defence counsel, and I believe he is prepared to withdraw the motion now based on this hearing today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honour. It is pointless now. My motive to write this was the fact that my request to attend the initial appeal was denied, and I received a written notification to that effect only a few days ago, and that's why I thought that this order was premature. In any case, it is now moot and I orally withdraw this motion. And one more thing, Your Honour. I don't want to impede on your time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just -- one second. It is on the record now that the motion for certification for appeal has been withdrawn. Please proceed, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The situation is clear as far as the disclosure is concerned. We are participants in the case, and we're duty-bound to keep the secret. And now we have come to the legal issue. What if a third party finds out what was going on? Are they under the same legal obligation as we are? This is going to be one of the issues in one of my motions, and this is what I wanted to say at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I may remind you that the indictment against your client, Mr. Jovic, has been confirmed. You know what is in this indictment. You could understand from that, that everyone, whether you find the information in the garbage bin, whether you find it anywhere else, that you're under a duty, that everyone is under a duty to not make any protective measure of this Tribunal without effect, and it's not -- let me leave it to that. Mr. Akerson, any further issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: No further issues from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any further issues by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This concludes this Initial Appearance. We stand adjourned sine die.
